title: Characterization of influenza A(H3N2) viruses detected on a pig farm in Russia in 2017-2018.
abstract: Pigs serve as "mixing vessels" for influenza A viruses, facilitating interspecies transmission and genomic reassortment. Here, we report characterization of influenza A(H3N2) viruses isolated from suckling and weaned piglets at one commercial pig farm in the Irkutsk Region, Russia, in August 2017 and May 2018. Full-genome sequencing revealed that their HA and NA segments clustered with human seasonal A(H3N2) strains circulating in 2002-2004, while the internal gene cassette was derived from A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses. PB1 and PB2 segments of viruses isolated in 2017 and 2018 belonged to different clusters of the A(H1N1)pdm09 lineage suggesting possible additional reassortment event. Hemagglutination inhibition assay and antigenic cartography demonstrated significant antigenic drift, with the swine isolates forming a discrete cluster ≥ 4 antigenic units distant from human seasonal A(H3N2) strains registered in 2007-2024. The viruses accumulated key substitutions, including HA1-A138S, associated with swine adaptation, yet retained full susceptibility to oseltamivir and zanamivir. Repeated detection of closely related reassortants at the same farm suggests their sustained circulation either within the farm or outside it, leading to reintroductions. Further studies are needed to understand the underlying mechanisms of this observation. Thus, our study identified a new genetic lineage of human-origin influenza A(H3N2) viruses in swine in Russia and highlighted once again that seasonal influenza viruses that stopped circulating in the human population long ago might remain undetected for years within swine and/or other unknown intermediate hosts, undergoing independent evolution and generating antigenically distinct variants that may evade pre-existing human immunity.

title: End-of-season influenza vaccine effectiveness against a(H3N2) and B/Victoria in Beijing, China, 2025/26 season.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to estimate the end-of-season influenza vaccine effectiveness (VE) against A(H3N2) and B/Victoria in the 2025/26 season in Beijing, China. METHODS: We used a test-negative design to assess influenza VE among outpatients with influenza-like illness (ILI) enrolled through the Beijing influenza sentinel virological surveillance system from September 2025 (week 40/2025) to May 2026 (week 21/2026). Cases were ILI patients who tested positive for influenza; controls were those who tested negative. The VE was estimated using non-conditional multiple logistic regression models, adjusting for age (modelled as a natural cubic spline), sex, presence of comorbidities, area of residence, and calendar week (modelled as a natural cubic spline). RESULTS: Among 20,749 ILI patients tested, 4875 (23.5%) were positive for influenza, with A(H3N2) and B/Victoria being the predominant strains. Adjusted VE was 26.4% (95% CI: 17.8 to 34.1) against any influenza, 22.2% (95% CI: 11.3 to 31.7) against A(H3N2), and 34.7% (95% CI: 19.6 to 47.0) against B/Victoria, with the highest VE observed in adults aged 18-59 years (53.0%, 95%CI: 37.0 to 64.9) against any influenza. The adjusted VE was similar for those vaccinated in 2025/26 only (38.7%, 95%CI: 15.6 to 55.5) or both 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons (35.1%, 95%CI: 16.5 to 49.6), but higher than those vaccinated in 2024/25 only (17.0%, 95%CI: -16.1 to 40.7) among B/Victoria. For A(H3N2), the VE point estimate was higher among those vaccinated in the 2025/26 season only (27.9%, 95%CI: 11.5 to 41.2) than among those vaccinated in both seasons (17.9%, 95%CI: 4.0 to 29.7) and 2024/25 only (-6.1%, 95%CI: -28.7 to 12.5). CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that seasonal vaccination reduced laboratory-confirmed influenza among outpatients by approximately a quarter, with higher VE in adults aged 18-59 years. VE estimates according to vaccination status over two consecutive seasons showed different patterns for A(H3N2) and B/Victoria. These real-world findings support the ongoing public health value of influenza vaccination and highlight the importance of continuous virological surveillance, prevention, and control policy.

title: A Synthetic Virology Platform for Rapid Prototyping of Influenza A Virus mutants
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

title_zh: 用于甲型流感病毒突变体快速原型制作的合成病毒学平台
source_body_en: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat, with the need for effective vaccines and antiviral therapies remaining a high priority. In vitro testing is paramount in studying novel IAV viruses and their immunogenicity. To address this need, we developed a synthetic virology approach to rapidly prototype and test IAV mutants with altered antigenic sites. By strategically inserting restriction sites within an ambisense plasmid, we generated a tool where we can seamlessly replace either 1) the full hemagglutinin (HA), 2) the HA globular head domain to generate head/stalk chimeras or 3) the five canonical antigenic sites. The cloning inserts can be computationally designed and artificially synthesized, enabling rescue of synthetic Influenza A viruses. Using this platform we rescued IAV H1N1, H3N2 & H5N1, and went on to prototype their respective antigenic site mutants & chimeric IAVs using viral genome sequence alone. This platform could be useful for generating vaccine seed strains or to study anti-viral immunity.

title: Comparison chart: Antiviral drugs for seasonal influenza.
abstract: Influenza is typically a self-limited illness, but complications including pneumonia, respiratory failure, and death can occur, especially in persons at increased risk (see Table 1). Influenza vaccination reduces the incidence of laboratory-confirmed influenza and the risk of complications associated with influenza illness. Annual vaccination should be offered to all persons ≥6 months old as long as influenza viruses are circulating in the community.
journal: The medical letter on drugs and therapeutics/The medical letter

title: Differentiating Avian and Seasonal Influenza Viruses in Wastewater by Digital PCR.
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5Nx) viruses, particularly clade 2.3.4.4b, pose substantial global health risks. We combined and piloted 2 duplex reverse transcription digital PCRs to discriminate between avian and seasonal influenza viruses in wastewater. This approach enabled rapid, strain-specific detection to reduce ambiguity in environmental surveillance for influenza viruses.

title: Epitope-guided optimization improves the protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines against seasonal influenza A(H3N2) virus.
abstract: Neuraminidase (NA) is increasingly recognized as a promising target antigen for improving the breadth and durability of influenza vaccines, yet NA-based mRNA vaccines remain comparatively unexplored relative to hemagglutinin-based approaches. Here, we applied a computationally guided NA antigen-design strategy to seasonal H3N2 influenza viruses and investigated whether epitope-guided optimization could improve the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines. NA-D3, an NA antigen designed based on the evolutionary characteristics of circulating H3N2 viruses, was first evaluated in an mRNA vaccine. This vaccine provided partial protection against H3N2 challenge and reduced viral replication in the lungs, although detectable neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) activity was not observed. To further improve NA antigen immunogenicity, predicted B- and T-cell epitopes were incorporated into the antigen design process, resulting in three sequentially optimized NA candidates, F0, F1, and F2. In a subsequent challenge experiment, F1 and F2 conferred complete protection, achieving 100% survival and significantly lower viral RNA levels and infectious viral titers in the lungs compared to controls. The optimized NA mRNA vaccines also induced detectable NAI activity against heterologous H3N2 viruses, albeit at relatively modest levels. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective potential of NA-based mRNA vaccination against H3N2 influenza viruses and establish iterative, epitope-guided strategy in NA antigen optimization - integrating computational prediction with experimental validation - as an effective approach for developing broadly protective NA-based mRNA vaccines.

Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective potential of NA-based mRNA vaccination against H3N2 influenza viruses and establish iterative, epitope-guided strategy in NA antigen optimization - integrating computational prediction with experimental validation - as an effective approach for developing broadly protective NA-based mRNA vaccines.

abstract_zh: 神经氨酸酶 (NA) 越来越被认为是一种有前景的靶抗原,可用于改善流感 疫苗 的广度和持久性,但相对于基于血凝素的方法,基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 仍未得到探索。在这里,我们将计算引导的 NA 抗原设计策略应用于季节性 H3N2 流感病毒,并研究表位引导的优化是否可以提高基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 的免疫原性和保护功效。NA-D3 是一种根据流行的 H3N2 病毒的进化特征设计的 NA 抗原,首先在 mRNA 疫苗 中进行评估。尽管没有观察到可检测的神经氨酸酶抑制 (NAI) 活性,但该 疫苗 提供了针对 H3N2 攻击的部分保护并减少了肺部病毒复制。为了进一步提高 NA 抗原的免疫原性,预测的 B 细胞和 T 细胞表位被纳入抗原设计过程中,从而产生了三个连续优化的 NA 候选物:F0、F1 和 F2。在随后的攻击实验中,F1 和 F2 提供了完全的保护,实现了 100% 的存活,并且与对照组相比,肺部的病毒 RNA 水平和传染性病毒滴度显着降低。优化的 NA mRNA 疫苗 还诱导了针对异源 H3N2 病毒的可检测 NAI 活性,尽管水平相对较低。总的来说,这些发现证明了基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗接种 对 H3N2 流感病毒的保护潜力,并在 NA 抗原优化中建立了迭代、表位引导的策略 - 将计算预测与实验验证相结合 - 作为开发广泛保护性的基于 NA 的 mRNA 疫苗 的有效方法。

title: Bovine myxovirus resistance protein (Mx)1, but not Mx2, mediates antiviral activity against human and avian influenza A viruses, including H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b.
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b viruses have recently infected dairy cows in the United States, raising concerns about human spillover. The antiviral roles of bovine host defense factors, including myxovirus resistance proteins (bMx1 and bMx2), remain relatively understudied. We examined bMx1/bMx2 induction in differentiated bovine cells following HPAI H5N1 infection and assessed their antiviral activity using overexpression, knockdown, and mutagenesis approaches. Both bMx1 and bMx2 were more strongly induced in mammary cells than in tracheal cells. Overexpression of bMx1, but not bMx2, significantly inhibited seasonal influenza A viruses (IAVs), low-pathogenic, and highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses, including H5N1 2.3.4.4b, but not influenza B viruses. Conversely, knockdown of bMx1 resulted in enhanced IAV growth. Further, bMx1 inhibited early stages of viral replication, acting to reduce viral transcription and subsequent steps in the viral replication cycle. Known mutations that reduce human MxA (hMxA) activity also impaired bMx1 function, and mutations in the viral nucleoprotein (NP) associated with resistance to hMxA also reduced virus sensitivity to bMx1. Furthermore, phylogenetic analysis showed that a small minority (>0.03%) of avian H5N1 2.3.4.4b viruses already carry some of these NP mutations. These findings suggest that while current H5N1 viruses largely remain susceptible to bMx1, viral evolution or opportunistic reassortment could drive Mx resistance and increase pandemic risk.IMPORTANCEHighly pathogenic avian influenza viruses have spilled over into dairy cows and have been circulating on dairy farms in the United States since 2024. The innate antiviral immune responses of cows to influenza viruses have not been extensively studied. In this study, we focused on Mx proteins, a key part of the innate immune defense system toward viruses. We specifically looked at bovine Mx proteins and demonstrated antiviral activity toward different influenza viruses, including the highly pathogenic strains. We also showed that the mechanism of antiviral activity of bovine Mx1 was very similar to that of the human equivalent MxA protein. Further, we found that a small minority of these avian viruses have mutations associated with resistance to both bovine Mx1 and human MxA proteins. Overall, this work highlights the elevated pandemic risk for highly pathogenic influenza viruses through continual circulation in cows, a mammalian species in close proximity to humans.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解牛粘病毒抗性蛋白(bMx1和bMx2)在应对高致病性禽流感(HPAI)H5N1分支2.3.4.4b病毒中的抗病毒药物作用,该病毒最近感染了美国的奶牛,引起了对人类跨物种溢出的担忧。知识差距在于牛对流感病毒的先天 抗病毒药物 免疫应答 的研究不足,特别是 Mx 蛋白的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及检查 HPAI H5N1 感染后分化牛细胞中 bMx1/bMx2 的诱导情况,并使用过表达、敲低和诱变方法评估其 抗病毒药物 活性。该研究是利用牛乳腺和气管细胞在体外进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法包括检查牛细胞中的 bMx1/bMx2 诱导、bMx1 和 bMx2 的过度表达、敲低和诱变,以及评估 抗病毒药物 针对不同流感病毒(包括 H5N1 2.3.4.4b)的活性。
elements_zh.main_results: bMx1 和 bMx2 在乳腺细胞中的诱导作用比在气管细胞中的诱导作用更强。bMx1 的过表达(而非 bMx2)显着抑制 季节性流感 A 病毒 (IAV)、低致病性和高致病性禽流感病毒,包括 H5N1 2.3.4.4b,但不能抑制 B 型流感病毒。bMx1 的敲低导致 IAV 生长增强。bMx1 抑制病毒复制的早期阶段,从而减少病毒转录和病毒复制周期的后续步骤。少数禽类 H5N1 2.3.4.4b 病毒已携带可降低 MxA 活性的 突变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,虽然目前的 H5N1 病毒在很大程度上仍然对 bMx1 敏感,但病毒 进化 或重配可能会导致 Mx 耐药性并增加大流行风险。牛Mx1的抗病毒药物活性机制与人类等效的MxA蛋白非常相似,并且少数禽类病毒具有与牛Mx1和人MxA蛋白的抗性相关的突变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这项工作强调了高致病性流感病毒通过在牛(一种与人类关系密切的哺乳动物物种)中持续传播而增加的大流行风险。这些发现对牛流感的 监测、诊断 和 治疗 以及潜在的人类 跨物种溢出 事件具有影响。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到实验的体外性质和牛细胞的使用的限制,可能无法完全代表体内情况。病毒 突变 分析的样本量较小,研究结果对其他流感病毒和物种的普遍性尚不确定。证据强度中等。

title: ADAR-mediated RNA editing of Influenza A virus genomes may be age-dependent and inversely correlates with viral load.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients. METHODS: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

title_zh: ADAR 介导的甲型流感病毒 基因组 的 RNA 编辑可能具有年龄依赖性,并且与病毒载量呈负相关。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Seasonal influenza epidemics cause significant mortality, especially among the elderly. Influenza A virus triggers the host innate immune system through various mechanisms. Human enzymes belonging to the group of RNA-acting adenosine deaminases (ADARs) play a role in the innate antiviral immune response, partly by inducing mutations in viral RNA. The effect of this mechanismin influenza A virus infection remains unexplained in humans. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the clinical impact of ADAR-induced mutations on influenza A virus in hospitalised patients. METHODS: Full-genome deep sequencing of Influenza A virus was performed on respiratory samples from 75 hospitalised, Influenza A(H3N2) virus infected patients, aged 41 to 95 years. ADAR-associated mutations in minor viral subpopulations were analysed in relation to demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: ADAR-associated mutations showed a significant inverse correlation with viral load (p < 0.0001) and age (p = 0.0051), especially in patients older than 75 years. The association between ADAR-associated mutations and viral load was independent of age, inflammation, and disease severity (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: We found an association between ADAR-induced mutations and viral load, which may indicate an antiviral function of ADAR on influenza A virus. The lower mutation rate and associated higher viral load in the elderly suggest an age-dependent reduced ADAR activity, which may contribute to increased disease severity.

title: Influenza A Virus at the Exhibition Swine‐Human Interface in the USA
abstract: INTRODUCTION: In the USA, zoonotic influenza A virus (IAV) transmission occurs frequently in youth who exhibit swine at agricultural competitions, presenting an ongoing pandemic risk. However, active surveillance in this high-risk human population is lacking. METHODS: To address this gap, we enrolled 711 youth participants at nine swine exhibitions during 2019-2021 and collected 700 nasal swabs and 400 serum samples. We assessed the neutralizing antibody titers of enrollees against eight influenza A H1 and H3 variant candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs) recommended by the World Health Organization. RESULTS: We found that the highest neutralizing titers are not necessarily associated with the specific viruses which are most prevalent in exhibition swine during the same time period. The geometric mean titers of the cohort were low against the Cluster IV-A (clade 3.1990.4.a) CVV, which we determined to be the most prevalent HA lineage circulating in exhibition swine during 2020-2021 based on simultaneous IAV surveillance in swine (n = 430 genome sequences). CONCLUSIONS: The relatively low neutralizing antibody levels in this high-risk population with intense exposure to livestock indicates that sustained outreach and monitoring is needed. Continued monitoring of IAVs in both swine and humans can inform viral risk assessments and provide considerations for candidate vaccine virus selection.

title: Cross-reactivity against drifted influenza A (H3N2) subclade K is predicted by pre-existing antibody signatures from recent vaccine targets
abstract: Abstract Seasonal influenza vaccine strains are selected months before the flu season begins, risking a vaccine mismatch. To that end, quickly predicting protection against newly emerged influenza strains is a public health preparedness need. Further, understanding immunological correlates of protection against mismatched targets is necessary for improving annual influenza vaccination compositions and/or platforms. Using a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach, we quantified predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort pre- and post-vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, during which the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K accounted for most influenza virus infections. This was done using the previous 10 years of vaccine targets, including the components of the 2025/2026 vaccination, as well as the 2026/2027 vaccine targets. We identified that H3N2 subclade K responders were predicted by baseline SNAb profiles, particularly to the H3N2 components of the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza vaccine. Systems serological analysis supported this at the multivariate level, with even greater accuracy in predicting mismatched responses from pre-vaccination humoral signatures. Lastly, we employed this approach to predict who would likely be high responders to the 2026/2027 influenza vaccine H1 component, and found that antibody features selected as predicting a strong neutralization response were disproportionately enriched for the H1 component of the 2025/2026 influenza vaccination. Our results support a model in which systems-based approaches can identify signatures predicting strong influenza vaccination responses before the influenza season begins.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Seasonal influenza vaccine strains are selected months before the flu season begins, risking a vaccine mismatch. This study aimed to address the need for predicting protection against newly emerged influenza strains.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach to quantify predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort pre- and post-vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, when the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K accounted for most influenza virus infections.
analysis.methods: Using a modified systems-predicted neutralizing antibody (SNAb) approach, the researchers quantified predicted influenza virus neutralization responses in a human cohort before and after vaccination during the 2025/2026 influenza season, which was dominated by the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K.
analysis.main_results: The study identified that H3N2 subclade K responders were predicted by baseline SNAb profiles, particularly to the H3N2 components of the 2024/2025 and 2025/2026 influenza vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that systems-based serological analysis can predict mismatched responses from pre-vaccination humoral signatures, supporting a model for identifying vaccination response signatures before the influenza season begins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform the development of systems-based approaches to improve influenza vaccine composition and predict individual responses to mismatched vaccine targets, enhancing public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by its reliance on a single influenza season's data and the potential for unmeasured confounding factors, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of systems-based serological analysis to predict immune responses against the vaccine-mismatched H3N2 subclade K during the 2025/2026 influenza season. The researchers used a modified SNAb approach to assess pre- and post-vaccination neutralization responses in a human cohort. They found that baseline SNAb profiles, particularly those targeting H3N2 components of previous vaccines, could predict responses to the mismatched subclade K. These results suggest that such systems-based methods can identify signatures that predict strong influenza vaccination responses before the season begins, offering a potential tool for improving vaccine composition and public health preparedness. However, the study's findings are based on a single season's data and may be subject to unmeasured confounding factors, limiting the generalizability of the results.

title: S100A4 facilitates influenza A virus replication by interacting with M2 in human alveolar epithelial cells
abstract: Influenza A virus (IAV) replication depends on host cells and is regulated by numerous host factors. Therefore, investigating and understanding the role of these host factors is a significant topic. In this study, we found the IAV replication was attenuated after host factor S100 calcium-binding protein A4 (S100A4) was knocked down with RNAi or knockout with CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology. Conversely, IAV replication was enhanced upon the overexpression in A549 cells. The interaction between S100A4 and the IAV M2 protein was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation. Meanwhile, confocal microscopy experiment demonstrated that the viral M2 protein co-localized with endogenous S100A4 in IAV-infected A549 cells. Truncation analysis confirmed that amino acids 45–62 of the M2 protein constitute the main interaction region with S100A4. Further study showed that viral entry was reduced after S100A4 deletion. And the polymerase activity was significantly decreased in S100A4-knockout A549 cells compared to that in wild-type A549 cells. The S100A4 overexpression resulted in the downregulation of IFN-β, while the mRNA levels of the interferon-stimulated genes ISG15 and BST2 were also significantly reduced. Therefore, the host factor S100A4 was a positive modulator of IAV replication and was involved in the viral entry, polymerase activity maintenance and innate immune regulation. Collectively, our findings shed new light on the molecular mechanisms governing IAV infection and suggest a previously underexplored avenue for antiviral therapeutic intervention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza A virus (IAV) replication depends on host cells and is regulated by numerous host factors. Therefore, investigating and understanding the role of these host factors is a significant topic.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the host factor S100A4 in influenza A virus (IAV) replication. The researchers found that knocking down or knocking out S100A4 in human alveolar epithelial cells (A549) attenuated IAV replication, while overexpression enhanced it. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed the interaction between S100A4 and the IAV M2 protein, and confocal microscopy showed their co-localization in infected cells. Truncation analysis identified the main interaction region of the M2 protein with S100A4. Further results indicated that S100A4 deletion reduced viral entry and significantly decreased polymerase activity. The study also found that S100A4 overexpression downregulated IFN-β and interferon-stimulated genes ISG15 and BST2. These findings suggest that S100A4 is a positive modulator of IAV replication, involved in viral entry, polymerase activity maintenance, and innate immune regulation. The study provides insights into the molecular mechanisms of IAV infection and highlights a potential target for antiviral interventions. However, the study was conducted in vitro, which may limit its applicability to in vivo conditions, and the evidence strength is moderate.

title: Identification of cis-Acting Elements that Regulate Influenza A Virus Segment 7 Differential mRNA Splicing
abstract: Influenza A virus segment 7 encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel from an unspliced primary transcript (mRNA1) and spliced mRNA2, respectively. Both proteins are essential for efficient virus replication, but the intrinsic sequences that determine segment 7 splicing balance are not fully defined. Here, we systematically investigated how conserved cis-acting splicing elements regulate segment splicing. We found that while the splice acceptor sequence is optimal, both potential upstream polypyrimidine tracts regulate splicing, with the 5' region acting positively and the 3' region negatively to maintain M1 expression. Nucleotide A713 is the most likely mRNA2 branch point, but potentially with redundancy from other local adenosines. Mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence showed that it is nearly optimal but that nucleotides 51 and 55 modestly downregulate splicing efficiency. Most introduced mutations that change splicing balance are nonsynonymous in M1. Nevertheless, polypyrimidine tract and branch point mutations that significantly perturbed M1:M2 balance resulted in viable viruses. In contrast, the splice donor sequence was largely intolerant of mutation. We conclude that M1:M2 balance is maintained via suboptimal splice donor and polypyrimidine tract splicing signals, with the latter allowing more evolutionary flexibility to vary the ratio and/or M1 sequence

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify cis-acting elements that regulate differential mRNA splicing of influenza A virus segment 7, which encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel from unspliced and spliced transcripts, respectively. The research was motivated by the need to understand the intrinsic sequences that determine the splicing balance between these two proteins.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a systematic investigation of how conserved cis-acting splicing elements regulate segment 7 splicing in influenza A virus. It focused on the balance between M1 and M2 expression, with no specific mention of study dates, centres, or sample size.
analysis.methods: The researchers performed mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence and analyzed the effects on splicing efficiency. They also examined the roles of potential upstream polypyrimidine tracts and the branch point in regulating splicing balance.
analysis.main_results: Mutagenesis of the mRNA2 splice donor sequence showed that it is nearly optimal, but nucleotides 51 and 55 modestly downregulate splicing efficiency. Additionally, the 5' region of the polypyrimidine tract acts positively, while the 3' region acts negatively to maintain M1 expression.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the M1:M2 balance is maintained through suboptimal splice donor and polypyrimidine tract splicing signals, with the latter providing more evolutionary flexibility to vary the ratio and/or M1 sequence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide insights into the molecular mechanisms that regulate mRNA splicing in influenza A virus, which could inform future studies on viral gene expression and potentially contribute to the development of targeted antiviral strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence and does not include detailed experimental results or statistical analyses. The evidence strength is moderate as the conclusions are based on mutagenesis and splicing signal analysis without further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the cis-acting elements that regulate differential mRNA splicing of influenza A virus segment 7, which encodes the M1 matrix protein and M2 ion channel. The research highlights the roles of the splice donor sequence and polypyrimidine tracts in maintaining the M1:M2 balance. The findings suggest that the balance is achieved through suboptimal splicing signals, with the polypyrimidine tract allowing more evolutionary flexibility. The study is based on mutagenesis experiments and abstract-level evidence, which provides moderate confidence in the conclusions. These results could inform future research on viral gene expression and potentially contribute to antiviral strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在鉴定调节甲型流感病毒片段 7 差异 mRNA 剪接的顺式作用元件,该片段分别编码来自未剪接和剪接转录本的 M1 基质蛋白和 M2 离子通道。这项研究的动机是需要了解决定这两种蛋白质之间剪接平衡的内在序列。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究系统地研究了甲型流感病毒中保守的顺式作用剪接元件如何调节第 7 段剪接。它侧重于 M1 和 M2 表达之间的平衡,没有具体提及研究日期、中心或样本量。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员对 mRNA2 剪接供体序列进行了诱变,并分析了对剪接效率的影响。他们还研究了潜在的上游多嘧啶束和分支点在调节剪接平衡中的作用。
elements_zh.main_results: mRNA2 剪接供体序列的诱变表明它几乎是最佳的,但核苷酸 51 和 55 适度下调剪接效率。此外,多嘧啶束的 5' 区域起正作用,而 3' 区域起负作用以维持 M1 表达。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,M1:M2 平衡是通过次优剪接供体和多嘧啶束剪接信号来维持的,后者提供了更多的进化灵活性来改变比率和/或 M1 序列。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了对甲型流感病毒中调节 mRNA 剪接的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来病毒基因表达的研究提供信息,并可能有助于开发靶向 抗病毒药物 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象级别的证据,不包括详细的实验结果或统计分析。证据强度中等,因为结论是基于诱变和剪接信号分析而没有进一步验证。

abstract_zh: 甲型流感病毒片段 7 分别编码来自未剪接初级转录物 (mRNA1) 和剪接 mRNA2 的 M1 基质蛋白和 M2 离子通道。这两种蛋白对于有效的病毒复制都是必需的,但决定片段 7 剪接平衡的内在序列尚未完全确定。在这里,我们系统地研究了保守的顺式作用剪接元件如何调节片段剪接。我们发现,虽然剪接受体序列是最佳的,但两个潜在的上游多嘧啶束都调节剪接,5'区域起正作用,3'区域起负作用以维持M1表达。核苷酸 A713 是最有可能的 mRNA2 分支点,但可能与其他局部腺苷存在冗余。mRNA2 剪接供体序列的诱变表明它几乎是最佳的,但核苷酸 51 和 55 适度下调剪接效率。大多数引入的改变拼接平衡的突变在M1中都是非同义的。然而,显着扰乱 M1:M2 平衡的多嘧啶束和分支点 突变 产生了存活的病毒。相反,剪接供体序列很大程度上不耐受 突变。我们得出的结论是,M1:M2 平衡是通过次优剪接供体和聚嘧啶束剪接信号来维持的,后者允许更大的进化灵活性来改变比率和/或 M1 序列

title: Influenza B Circulation and Vaccine Effectiveness Against Medically Attended Outpatient Influenza B Illness, United States, 2016-17 Through 2024-25.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Influenza B vaccine effectiveness (VE) has varied by season, lineage, antigenic drift, and vaccine composition. After B/Yamagata detection ceased globally, trivalent vaccines containing B/Victoria were reintroduced in 2024-25. We evaluated influenza B circulation and VE across eight analyzed seasons spanning this transition. METHODS: Ambulatory patients aged ≥6 months with acute respiratory illness were enrolled at U.S. Flu VE Network sites during eight influenza seasons from 2016-17 through 2024-25; 2020-21 was excluded because influenza circulation was negligible. Participants were tested by RT-PCR. Lineage-specific VE was estimated using a test-negative design and logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, calendar time, and study site. VE was reported for season-lineage strata with ≥50 influenza B cases. RESULTS: Among 65,773 participants, 3,629 influenza B cases were included in lineage-specific VE analyses (1,507 B/Yamagata; 2,122 B/Victoria). Six of 10 season-lineage strata met the reporting threshold. B/Victoria VE was 58% (95% CI, 28%-77%) in 2016-17, 51% (43%-57%) in 2019-20, 78% (71%-84%) in 2023-24, and 39% (14%-56%) in 2024-25. B/Yamagata VE was 55% (46%-63%) in 2016-17 and 49% (40%-56%) in 2017-18. CONCLUSIONS: Influenza vaccines protected against medically attended outpatient influenza B illness, although VE varied by season. Continued VE monitoring and genetic surveillance are needed to detect emerging influenza B viruses and inform vaccine strain selection.

abstract_zh: 背景:流感B病毒株的疫苗有效性(VE)在不同季节、谱系、抗原漂移和疫苗组成方面有所不同。在B/Yamagata病毒株全球检测停止后,含有B/Victoria病毒株的三价疫苗于2024-25赛季重新引入。我们评估了流感B病毒的传播情况以及在这一转变期间的八个分析季节中的疫苗有效性。方法:在2016-17至2024-25年的八个流感季节中,美国流感疫苗有效性网络站点招募了年龄≥6个月且患有急性呼吸道疾病的门诊患者;由于2020-21年流感传播量极少,该年份被排除。参与者通过RT-PCR进行检测。使用测试阴性设计和调整年龄、性别、种族/民族、日历时间和研究地点的逻辑回归分析,估计了特定谱系的疫苗有效性。对于流感B病例≥50的季节-谱系分层,报告了疫苗有效性结果。结果:在65,773名参与者中,有3,629例流感B病例纳入谱系特异性疫苗有效性分析(1,507例B/Yamagata;2,122例B/Victoria)。10个季节-谱系分层中有6个达到报告阈值。2016-17年B/Victoria病毒株的疫苗有效性为58%(95%置信区间,28%-77%),2019-20年为51%(43%-57%),2023-24年为78%(71%-84%),2024-25年为39%(14%-56%)。2016-17年和2017-18年B/Yamagata病毒株的疫苗有效性分别为55%(46%-63%)和49%(40%-56%)。结论:流感疫苗对需要医疗干预的流感B门诊病例提供了保护,尽管疫苗有效性在不同季节有所变化。需要持续监测疫苗有效性并进行遗传监测,以检测新兴的流感B病毒株并为疫苗株选择提供信息。

title: More Shots on Goal: Heterologous Influenza Prime-Boost Vaccination Decreases the Likelihood of a Negligible Antibody Response to Current or Historical Variants
abstract: Seasonal influenza vaccination only elicits a strong and durable antibody response in a subset of recipients, and prior homologous booster trials have failed to improve on single-dose vaccination. Here, we conducted a phase 4 clinical trial to test if a heterologous prime-boost increases antibody magnitude or breadth as well as reduces the rate of non-responders (ClinicalTrials.gov ID# NCT06567860). Participants received a late-season 2023 inactivated influenza vaccine followed by the 2024 booster four months later containing an updated H3N2 strain alongside unchanged H1N1 and B/Victoria strains, allowing within-subject comparison of heterologous and homologous boosting. The booster vaccination halted or reversed antibody titer waning for all vaccine strains, most notably restoring seroprotective and seroconverting titers for B/Victoria at the cohort-level. analysis.summary_en: This study investigates whether a heterologous prime-boost vaccination strategy can improve antibody responses to seasonal influenza variants. The research highlights that seasonal influenza vaccination only elicits strong and durable responses in a subset of individuals, and prior homologous booster trials have not improved single-dose efficacy. A phase 4 clinical trial was conducted, where participants received a late-season 2023 vaccine followed by a 2024 booster with an updated H3N2 strain and unchanged H1N1 and B/Victoria strains. The results showed that the heterologous booster significantly reduced the rate of non-responders, with 0% non-responders for H3N2 compared to 29% for H1N1. The findings suggest that heterologous vaccinations may enhance antibody responses, particularly against updated strains. The study's implications indicate that this approach could improve vaccine effectiveness, especially when cohorts are matched on pre-vaccination titers. However, the evidence does not address long-term efficacy or safety, which limits the strength of the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 季节性流感 疫苗接种 仅在一部分受者中引起强烈且持久的抗体反应,之前的同源加强试验未能改善单剂量 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在这里,我们进行了一项 4 期临床试验,以测试异源初免-加强是否会增加抗体的强度或宽度以及降低无反应率(ClinicalTrials.gov ID# NCT06567860)。
elements_zh.methods: 参与者接受了 2023 年末季灭活流感 疫苗,四个月后又接受了 2024 年加强疫苗,其中包含更新的 H3N2 毒株以及未改变的 H1N1 和 B/Victoria 毒株,从而可以在受试者内比较异源和同源加强疫苗。
elements_zh.main_results: 至关重要的是,异源加强剂降低了无反应者的比例(在所有时间点均表现出 HAI[≤]10),接受初免和加强剂的受试者中 H3N2 无反应者为 0%,而 H1N1 无反应者为 29%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,异源 疫苗接种 或其他多毒株暴露可以减少在流感季节期间未产生抗体反应的人群比例。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 尽管 疫苗接种 时间不同,但当 队列研究 与 疫苗接种 前滴度匹配时,季末启动和标准秋季 疫苗接种 在 疫苗接种 后 30 天产生了相当的抗体宽度。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告异源初免-加强策略的长期疗效或安全性。

abstract_zh: 季节性流感 疫苗接种 仅在一部分受者中引起强烈且持久的抗体反应,之前的同源加强试验未能改善单剂量 疫苗接种。在这里,我们进行了一项 4 期临床试验,以测试异源初免-加强是否会增加抗体的强度或宽度以及降低无反应率(ClinicalTrials.gov ID# NCT06567860)。参与者接受了 2023 年末季灭活流感 疫苗,四个月后又接受了 2024 年加强疫苗,其中包含更新的 H3N2 毒株以及未改变的 H1N1 和 B/Victoria 毒株,从而可以在受试者内比较异源和同源加强疫苗。加强剂 疫苗接种 停止或逆转了所有 疫苗 菌株的抗体滴度减弱,最显着的是恢复了 B/Victoria 的 队列研究 水平的血清保护和血清转换滴度。至关重要的是,异源加强剂降低了无反应者的比例(在所有时间点均表现出 HAI[≤]10),接受初免和加强剂的受试者中 H3N2 无反应者为 0%,而 H1N1 无反应者为 29%。在连续秋季服用 队列研究 的较大 队列研究 中也存在类似的模式,其中 H3N2 的无反应率为 20%,而 H1N1 的无反应率为 37%。在所有对 疫苗 菌株滴度始终较低的无应答者中,多达一半引发了针对历史变体的抗体应答,这表明免疫印记部分是无应答者表型的基础。尽管 疫苗接种 时间不同,但当 队列研究 与 疫苗接种 前滴度匹配时,季末启动和标准秋季 疫苗接种 在 疫苗接种 后 30 天产生了相当的抗体宽度。这些发现表明,异源 疫苗接种 或其他多毒株暴露可以减少在流感季节期间未产生抗体反应的人群比例。

title: Sequence-structured fitness landscapes predict influenza evolution
abstract: Seasonal influenza viruses continually evolve to evade host immunity. Vaccines must be regularly updated to protect against new circulating strains, motivating efforts to forecast viral evolution. Recent experimental and computational methods have made progress on this problem, but learning the fitness landscape driving viral evolution remains challenging because genomic surveillance samples only a small fraction of the possible sequence space. Here, we developed a generative framework that shares information across genetically related variants, inferring effective mutation-level contributions to viral fitness from temporal sequence data. Applied to hemagglutinin and neuraminidase from A/H3N2 and A/H1N1 viruses, the inferred fitness landscapes recovers known determinants of antigenicity and reveals convergent spatial organization across subtypes consistent with common antibody-mediated selection. Forward simulations from these landscapes predicted both the fixation or loss of circulating mutations and the future composition of viral populations, outperforming models based on neutral evolution or multinomial-logistic growth. Collectively, our results show that interpretable representations of pathogen fitness landscapes can reveal biologically important features and improve prospective evolutionary forecasting.

title: Influenza H1N1 Imprinting Uncouples Serological and B-Cell Responses in Mice
abstract: Antigenic drift reduces the protective potential of antibodies generated against earlier influenza variants. Unfortunately, a new infection or vaccination often preferentially recalls antibodies targeting previously encountered strains, thereby limiting responses to newly emerged variants. Although this phenomenon, known as immunological imprinting, has been well documented at the serological level, its underlying cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To resolve imprinting at both the serological and cellular level, we combined serum antibody profiling with targeted B-cell characterization in mice, including single-cell B-cell receptor (BCR) sequencing of germinal center (GC) B cells following secondary H1N1 challenge and bulk BCR sequencing of bone marrow plasma cells. We found that a primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 ("swine flu") strain largely prevented the generation of new serum antibodies following secondary exposure to the antigenically distinct H1N1 strain A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8), whereas the reciprocal infection sequence updated antibody specificities towards the last encountered virus. GC B cells did not mirror serological imprinting and instead generated updated BCR repertoires directed against the heterologous challenge strain. Likewise, BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells failed to mirror the serological imprinting observed in the antibody response. Together, these findings reveal a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide the development of improved seasonal influenza vaccines across a diverse population.

GC B cells did not mirror serological imprinting and instead generated updated BCR repertoires directed against the heterologous challenge strain. Likewise, BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells failed to mirror the serological imprinting observed in the antibody response. Together, these findings reveal a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide the development of improved seasonal influenza vaccines across a diverse population.

title: Genomic Surveillance and Evolution of Influenza Virus Across Two Consecutive Seasons, 2024–2026, in Southern Greece
abstract: Continuous genomic surveillance of influenza virus is critical for monitoring viral evolution, detecting emerging variants, and informing vaccine strain selection. While partial-gene Sanger sequencing has traditionally underpinned national surveillance programs, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) enables simultaneous characterization of all eight genomic segments, providing resolution not achievable through conventional approaches. This is the first published, systematic, whole-genome-based influenza surveillance study reported from Greece. We sequenced and characterized influenza viruses circulating in Southern Greece (S. Greece) during two consecutive influenza seasons, 2024–2025 and 2025–2026, using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) sequencing. A total of 40 samples were analyzed, with complete or near-complete genome assembly achieved in the vast majority of them. During 2024–2025, co-circulation of A(H1N1)pdm09 (subclades C.1.9.3 and D.3.1), A(H3N2) (subclades J.1.1 and J.2.2), and B/Victoria (C.5 subclades, predominantly C.5.7) influenza viruses was confirmed, with the detection of an oseltamivir-resistant H1N1 variant carrying NA H275Y as a clinically significant finding. Extension of surveillance into 2025–2026 revealed a complete inter-seasonal lineage transition in A(H1N1)pdm09 from subclade C.1.9.3 to D.3.1/D.3.1.1, and the rapid emergence and geographic dissemination of A(H3N2) subclade K across multiple regions of Southern Greece. Phylogenetic analysis characterized the HA subclade composition across the two seasons and positioned the Greek strains within the European and global context. Sequences of subclade K strains from S. Greece were phylogenetically concordant with the updated 2026–2027 vaccine strains, in line with ECDC and WHO surveillance data. Whole-genome analysis confirmed the absence of virulence-associated polymerase markers in all isolates with fully assembled polymerase segments, and identified conserved internal segment substitution patterns co-segregating with circulating subclades. These findings provide the first published whole-genome evolutionary dataset for influenza in Southern Greece, contributing insight into subtype and clade-level evolutionary dynamics and demonstrating the public health value of sustained genomic surveillance at a national reference laboratory level.

Greek) 传播的流感病毒进行了测序和特征分析。总共分析了 40 个样品,其中绝大多数实现了完整或接近完整的 基因组 组装。2024-2025年期间,通过检测到携带NA的奥司他韦耐药H1N1变种,证实了甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09(亚进化枝C.1.9.3和D.3.1)、甲型H3N2流感病毒(亚进化枝J.1.1和J.2.2)和B/Victoria(C.5亚进化枝,主要是C.5.7)流感病毒的共同传播H275Y 是一项具有临床意义的发现。监测 延伸至 2025-2026 年揭示了 甲型H1N1流感病毒pdm09 从分支 C.1.9.3 到 D.3.1/D.3.1.1 的完整季节间谱系转变,以及 甲型H3N2流感病毒 分支 K 在希腊南部多个地区的快速出现和地理传播。系统发育分析表征了两个季节的 HA 分支组成,并将希腊菌株定位在欧洲和全球背景下。来自希腊南部的 K 亚支菌株的序列在系统发育上与更新的 2026-2027 疫苗 菌株一致,与 ECDC 和 WHO 监测 数据一致。Whole-基因组 分析证实,在具有完全组装的聚合酶片段的所有分离株中不存在毒力相关聚合酶标记,并鉴定了与循环亚进化枝共分离的保守内部片段取代模式。这些发现提供了第一个发布的希腊南部流感的全 基因组 进化数据集,有助于深入了解亚型和分支水平的进化动态,并在国家参考实验室水平证明持续 基因组监测 的公共卫生价值。

title: Genomic and Clinical Analysis of Influenza A in Hospitalized Adults, 2019-2024: Exploratory Evidence on Neuraminidase and Polymerase Acidic Protein Mutation-Outcome Associations From a Single Center.
abstract: Background Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period. Conclusions Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the association between specific neuraminidase (NA) and polymerase acidic (PA) mutations and clinical outcomes in hospitalized adults with influenza A virus infection. Conducted at Ruijin Hospital in Shanghai between 2019 and 2024, the study analyzed 765 patients with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A. The findings revealed that older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, while antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Although some mutations showed an exploratory association with prolonged length of stay, these findings were confounded by clade and calendar period. The study concluded that clinical outcomes were primarily driven by host factors and admission severity, and that the associations between NA/PA mutations and outcomes require further validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 抗病毒药物被广泛用于治疗流感,但潜在耐药性突变仍然是一个重大挑战,并且关键耐药性突变的临床数据有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们对 2019 年至 2024 年间上海瑞金医院收治的 765 名经 RT-PCR 确诊的甲型流感成人患者进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,以确定在与关键 宿主 因素一起分析时,特定的 NA/PA 队列研究 是否与严重后果或住院时间延长 (LOS) 相关。
elements_zh.methods: 获得 PA 和 NA 序列并将其与临床 队列研究 关联以进行 突变 临床结果分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 765名甲型流感病毒感染住院患者中,中位年龄为68岁;5.0%为重症,9.9%死亡。主要高层阻力位突变不存在;检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重疾病或 死亡率 没有显着相关性。PA-F105L 显示出与较长 LOS 的探索性关联,但这一发现在调整后减弱,并且受到进化枝和日历周期的混淆。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 年龄较大、较高的 CURB-65 评分和细菌/真菌合并感染是 死亡率 的主要相关因素,而 抗病毒药物 方案和 Ct 值与 死亡率 或严重结局不独立相关。检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重后果没有显着相关性,同时无法评估高水平耐药性;PA-F105L-LOS 关联需要表型和外部验证。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 临床结果主要由 宿主 因素和入院严重程度决定。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 通过使用 Benjamini-Hochberg 程序控制错误发现率来解决多重测试问题。提供的证据没有报告与研究设计或人群相关的任何具体限制。

title_zh: 2019-2024 年住院成人甲型流感的基因组和临床分析:来自单中心的神经氨酸酶和聚合酶酸性蛋白 突变 结果关联的探索性证据。
source_body_en: Background Antivirals are widely used to treat influenza, but potential resistance mutations remain a major challenge, and clinical data on key resistance mutations are limited. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 765 adults with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza A admitted to Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, between 2019 and 2024 to determine whether specific NA/PA mutations are associated with severe outcomes or prolonged length of stay (LOS) when analyzed alongside key host factors. PA and NA sequences were obtained and linked to the clinical cohort for mutation-clinical outcome analyses. Multiple testing was addressed by controlling the false discovery rate using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. Results Among 765 inpatients with influenza A virus infection, the median age was 68 years; 5.0% were severe disease and 9.9% died. Older age, higher CURB-65 score, and bacterial/fungal co-infection were the main correlates of mortality, whereas antiviral regimen and Ct value were not independently associated with mortality or severe outcomes. Adjusted observational analyses showed a lower estimate for severe disease with baloxavir but no association with in-hospital death. Major high-level resistance mutations were absent; detected NA/PA mutations showed no robust association with severe disease or mortality. PA-F105L showed an exploratory association with longer LOS, but this finding was attenuated after adjustment and was confounded by clade and calendar period. Conclusions Clinical outcomes were driven mainly by host factors and admission severity. Detected NA/PA mutations were not robustly associated with severe outcomes, while high-level resistance could not be assessed; PA-F105L-LOS association requires phenotypic and external validation.
abstract_zh: 背景 抗病毒药物 被广泛用于治疗流感,但潜在耐药性 突变 仍然是一个重大挑战,并且关键耐药性 突变 的临床数据有限。方法 我们对 2019 年至 2024 年间上海瑞金医院收治的 765 名经 RT-PCR 确诊的甲型流感成人患者进行了回顾性 队列研究 研究,以确定在与关键 宿主 因素一起分析时,特定的 NA/PA 队列研究 是否与严重结局或住院时间延长 (LOS) 相关。获得 PA 和 NA 序列并将其与临床 队列研究 关联以进行 突变 临床结果分析。通过使用 Benjamini-Hochberg 程序控制错误发现率来解决多重测试问题。结果 765例甲型流感病毒感染住院患者中,中位年龄为68岁;5.0%为重症,9.9%死亡。年龄较大、较高的 CURB-65 评分和细菌/真菌合并感染是 死亡率 的主要相关因素,而 抗病毒药物 方案和 Ct 值与 死亡率 或严重结局不独立相关。调整后的观察分析显示,巴洛沙韦对严重疾病的估计较低,但与院内死亡无关。主要高层阻力位突变不存在;检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重疾病或 死亡率 没有显着相关性。PA-F105L 显示出与较长 LOS 的探索性关联,但这一发现在调整后减弱,并且受到进化枝和日历周期的混淆。结论 临床结果主要由 宿主 因素和入院严重程度决定。检测到的 NA/PA 突变 与严重后果没有显着相关性,同时无法评估高水平耐药性;PA-F105L-LOS 关联需要表型和外部验证。

title: Earth-Abundant Kaolin Derived Antiviral Coating via Triple Synergistic Capture-Inactivate-Block Mechanism.
abstract: Antiviral coating translation is constrained by additive aggregation and resin incompatibility. We upgrade natural kaolin into an efficient antiviral additive via thermal activation and one-pot ball milling with copper precursors, yielding amorphous metakaolin uniformly decorated with copper particles (Cu Ps). This solvent-free protocol suppresses Cu Ps agglomeration and ensures homogeneous dispersion within silicone-acrylic binders, essential for coating integrity. The metakaolin scaffold serves as a high-affinity viral capture platform, while anchored Cu Ps synergistically generate superoxide radicals (•O2-) and sustain localized Cu+/Cu2+ release, enabling dual-modal oxidative inactivation. Combined with the resin's physical barrier, this capture-oxidize-block mechanism delivers >99.9% inactivation of influenza A H3N2 and enterovirus EV-71 under ambient conditions. The composite supports kilogram-scale production (2.22 kg batch), maintains full activity after >6000 washing cycles, and passes dermal safety tests. This work transforms a low-cost clay mineral into a structurally engineered antiviral material and provides a scalable route that overcomes persistent manufacturability and durability limitations in surface protection.

title: Temporal Shifting of Influenza Subtype Dynamics in Pakistan Following the COVID-19 Pandemic: A 10-Year FluNet Analysis, 2015-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions caused unprecedented suppression of influenza circulation globally. Pakistan, with its high population density and evolving surveillance capacity, lacks long-term data on post-COVID-19 influenza patterns, essential for guiding vaccine policy. METHODS: We extracted weekly virological data for Pakistan from the WHO FluNet platform (January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024). The study period was divided into pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024) phases. Outcomes included type A versus B proportion, subtype distribution (A[H1N1]pdm09 vs. A[H3]), positivity, peak intensity, and season duration (weeks with positivity ≥ 10%). Statistical comparisons used chi-square for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis for peak intensity. RESULTS: We analyzed 6522 positive specimens from 79,484 tested (10,781 pre-COVID-19; 14,687 during COVID-19 disruption; 54,016 post-COVID-19). Influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% then rose to 77.5%; influenza B increased from 5.7% to 28.3%, remaining at 22.5% (p < 0.001). A(H3) dominated during the COVID-19 disruption (98.8%); A(H1N1)pdm09 regained dominance post-COVID-19 (58.8%), though A(H3) remained higher than pre-COVID-19 (41.2% vs. Peak intensity differed (p = 0.047): pre-COVID-19 33.3%-67.6%; COVID-19 disruption 14.0%-17.6%; and post-COVID-19 19.8%-37.8%. Season duration was 1 week in 2020 and 3 non-consecutive weeks in 2021, versus 10-16 weeks pre-COVID-19, recovering to 7-13 weeks post-COVID-19. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic induced a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with persistently elevated influenza B and reshaped A subtype balance. These findings are consistent with the global disappearance of B/Yamagata and support consideration of trivalent vaccine formulations, though antigenic and genetic data remain necessary to confirm vaccine match.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate how the COVID-19 pandemic affected influenza circulation in Pakistan, particularly focusing on the shift in subtype dynamics. The background highlights that the pandemic and its interventions led to a global suppression of influenza activity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed weekly virological data from the WHO FluNet platform in Pakistan, covering the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024. It divided the data into three phases: pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024).
analysis.methods: The researchers extracted virological data and categorized outcomes such as subtype distribution, positivity, peak intensity, and season duration. They used chi-square tests for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis tests for peak intensity comparisons.
analysis.main_results: The study found that influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% during the pandemic and then increased to 77.5%. Influenza B increased from 5.7% to 28.3%, remaining at 22.5% (p < 0.001). A(H3) dominated during the pandemic, while A(H1N1)pdm09 regained dominance afterward. Peak intensity varied across phases, and season duration was shorter during the pandemic compared to pre- and post-pandemic periods.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that the pandemic caused a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with increased influenza B and changes in the balance between A subtypes. This aligns with global trends of B/Yamagata disappearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that vaccine policy in Pakistan should consider the altered influenza dynamics, particularly the increased prevalence of influenza B and the need for trivalent vaccine formulations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on abstract-only data, which may limit the depth of analysis. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on observational trends without detailed mechanistic or causal explanations.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on influenza dynamics in Pakistan using a 10-year dataset from the WHO FluNet platform. It identifies a significant shift in the proportion of influenza A and B subtypes, with influenza B increasing and A(H1N1)pdm09 regaining dominance post-pandemic. The findings suggest a lasting change in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, consistent with global trends of B/Yamagata decline. These results have implications for vaccine formulation and policy, though further antigenic and genetic data are needed to confirm vaccine match. The study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on observational data without detailed causal mechanisms.

title_zh: COVID-19 大流行后巴基斯坦流感亚型动态的时间变化:2015-2024 年 10 年 FluNet 分析。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated nonpharmaceutical interventions caused unprecedented suppression of influenza circulation globally. Pakistan, with its high population density and evolving surveillance capacity, lacks long-term data on post-COVID-19 influenza patterns, essential for guiding vaccine policy. METHODS: We extracted weekly virological data for Pakistan from the WHO FluNet platform (January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2024). The study period was divided into pre-COVID-19 (2015-2019), COVID-19 disruption (2020-2021), and post-COVID-19 (2022-2024) phases. Outcomes included type A versus B proportion, subtype distribution (A[H1N1]pdm09 vs. A[H3]), positivity, peak intensity, and season duration (weeks with positivity ≥ 10%). Statistical comparisons used chi-square for subtype distribution and Kruskal-Wallis for peak intensity. RESULTS: We analyzed 6522 positive specimens from 79,484 tested (10,781 pre-COVID-19; 14,687 during COVID-19 disruption; 54,016 post-COVID-19). Influenza A declined from 94.2% to 71.7% then rose to 77.5%; influenza B increased from 5.7% to 28.3%, remaining at 22.5% (p < 0.001). A(H3) dominated during the COVID-19 disruption (98.8%); A(H1N1)pdm09 regained dominance post-COVID-19 (58.8%), though A(H3) remained higher than pre-COVID-19 (41.2% vs. Peak intensity differed (p = 0.047): pre-COVID-19 33.3%-67.6%; COVID-19 disruption 14.0%-17.6%; and post-COVID-19 19.8%-37.8%. Season duration was 1 week in 2020 and 3 non-consecutive weeks in 2021, versus 10-16 weeks pre-COVID-19, recovering to 7-13 weeks post-COVID-19. CONCLUSION: The COVID-19 pandemic induced a lasting shift in Pakistan's influenza epidemiology, with persistently elevated influenza B and reshaped A subtype balance. These findings are consistent with the global disappearance of B/Yamagata and support consideration of trivalent vaccine formulations, though antigenic and genetic data remain necessary to confirm vaccine match.

title: Systematic Literature Review: Distribution and Diversity of Avian Influenza Subtypes in Migratory Wild Birds in Asia and Australia
abstract: Avian influenza A viruses (AIVs) have been detected in migratory wild birds, raising concerns regarding their geographic distribution, subtype diversity, and surveillance along the East Asian–Australasian Flyway. This systematic literature review synthesized findings from studies investigating AIVs in migratory wild birds across Asia and Australia. Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, resulting in 29 eligible articles selected according to predefined inclusion criteria. The synthesis examined reported geographic locations, avian host groups, viral subtypes, diagnostic methods, and prevalence estimates. The included studies documented AIV detections in China, South Korea, Japan, Bangladesh, Siberian Russia, and Australia, predominantly among species belonging to the orders Anseriformes and Charadriiformes. Multiple hemagglutinin (HA) and neuraminidase (NA) subtype combinations were identified, including viruses belonging to the H5, H6, H4, H3, and H7 hemagglutinin subtype groups. Common diagnostic approaches included reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), quantitative reverse transcription PCR (RT-qPCR), virus isolation, genomic sequencing, and phylogenetic analysis. Reported detection positivity rates and prevalence estimates varied considerably, with many studies reporting values below 10%. However, differences in sampling strategies, sample denominators, and laboratory methods limited direct comparisons across studies. The observed geographic patterns reflected the distribution of published surveillance activities rather than the complete geographic distribution of AIVs, while viral detection alone did not establish cross-regional transmission by individual migratory birds. The findings highlighted the importance of standardized surveillance protocols and integrated One Health monitoring to improve understanding of AIV distribution and subtype diversity. Furthermore, inconsistencies in reported sample denominators and subtype counts underscored the need for careful verification and harmonization of extracted data to strengthen the reliability of future surveillance syntheses.

title: N1 neuraminidase monoclonal antibodies 2H08 and 3H03 have decreased binding and inhibition properties against H1N1 influenza viruses circulating after 2018
abstract: Abstract Influenza viruses are global public health problem. Vaccines are available but have to be updated annually due to antigenic drift of the main vaccine component, the surface glycoprotein hemagglutinin (HA). The second surface glycoprotein of the virus, neuraminidase (NA), has recently moved into the spotlight of vaccine development. However, its antigenic evolution is understudied. We found that two broadly protective N1 NA antibodies, which had previously been shown to bind and inhibit most N1 NA, lost activity to recent N1s from seasonal H1N1 viruses. Here, we show that this drop in activity can mostly be attributed to a change in electrostatic surface potential from neutral to positively charged. This effect was not observed when historic human plasma samples were tested, suggesting that the drop of activity is specific to the two tested mAbs but does not broadly impact the polyclonal human response. Finally, we confirmed that the tested mAbs were fully active against recently emerged panzootic clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 NA. Importance The influenza virus NA has become an important target for vaccine development. The characterization of antigenic changes described in this manuscript contributes to our understanding of conservation of epitopes in NA.

The second surface glycoprotein of the virus, neuraminidase (NA), has recently moved into the spotlight of vaccine development. However, its antigenic evolution is understudied. We found that two broadly protective N1 NA antibodies, which had previously been shown to bind and inhibit most N1 NA, lost activity to recent N1s from seasonal H1N1 viruses. Here, we show that this drop in activity can mostly be attributed to a change in electrostatic surface potential from neutral to positively charged. This effect was not observed when historic human plasma samples were tested, suggesting that the drop of activity is specific to the two tested mAbs but does not broadly impact the polyclonal human response. Finally, we confirmed that the tested mAbs were fully active against recently emerged panzootic clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 NA. Importance The influenza virus NA has become an important target for vaccine development. The characterization of antigenic changes described in this manuscript contributes to our understanding of conservation of epitopes in NA.

title: Population attributable mortality associated with respiratory viruses in Ontario, Canada: a population-based ecological analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory viruses are major contributors to population mortality, but cause-of-death coding undercounts their impact. Ecological regression models linking viral circulation to mortality fluctuations can address this limitation. Aim To estimate the population attributable fraction (PAF) of mortality associated with influenza A and B, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 in Ontario, Canada (1993–2025), and to characterize temporal changes in virus-attributable mortality across the pandemic transition. Methods We analysed monthly all-cause mortality data with laboratory surveillance indicators for influenza A, B, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2. Negative binomial models with secular trends, Fourier seasonal terms, and population offsets were fit for pre-pandemic (January 1993–February 2020) and combined pandemic (March 2020–February 2025) periods. PAFs were derived from counterfactual predictions setting viral coefficients to zero. Sensitivity analyses examined temporal stratification of the pandemic period (Public Health Emergency of International Concern [PHEIC] period: March 2020–April 2023; post-PHEIC: May 2023–February 2025), exclusion of the early pandemic period (March–June 2020), and models without Fourier seasonal adjustment. Wald tests compared coefficients across specifications. Results Pre-pandemic, influenza A accounted for 1.8% (95% CI 1.4–2.3%) of mortality; influenza B showed no detectable impact. RSV demonstrated inverse associations in seasonally adjusted models but positive associations (PAF 1.9%, 95% CI 1.3–2.4%) without seasonal adjustment. Over the combined pandemic period (March 2020–February 2025; n=60 months), amid elevated baseline mortality (IRR 1.050, P=0.027), SARS-CoV-2 accounted for 6.1% (95% CI 4.2–8.0%) of deaths, approximately 4-fold the pre-pandemic influenza A burden, despite widespread vaccination and antiviral availability. Model-estimated SARS-CoV-2-attributable deaths closely matched reported COVID-19 deaths from Public Health Ontario over the same period. Temporal stratification identified a significant increase in SARS-CoV-2-attributable mortality in the post-PHEIC period (PAF 9.8%, 95% CI 1.1–17.7%; p=0.027), while post-PHEIC influenza A and B attributable fractions did not differ significantly from pre-pandemic baselines. Excluding March-June 2020 yielded a conservative SARS-CoV-2 PAF of 5.7% (95% CI 3.3–8.1%), confirming robustness of primary estimates. Meta-analyses showed substantial heterogeneity for influenza A (I2=92.8%) and RSV (I2=89.1%) across modeling approaches, but minimal heterogeneity for SARS-CoV-2 (I2=5.5%). Conclusion SARS-CoV-2 was associated with a 3–4-fold higher population mortality burden than seasonal influenza A despite available countermeasures. Post-PHEIC data suggest that the burden of respiratory virus mortality, including for influenza, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, highlighting the continued importance of respiratory virus prevention strategies. Estimates for influenza A and RSV were sensitive to seasonal adjustment, highlighting the importance of modelling choices when quantifying virus-attributable mortality.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒是 死亡率 群体的主要贡献者,但死因编码低估了其影响。该研究旨在估计与特定呼吸道病毒相关的 死亡率 的人群归因分数。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 1993 年 1 月至 2025 年 2 月加拿大安大略省每月全因 死亡率 数据进行了生态分析。该研究重点关注甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2。
elements_zh.methods: 使用具有长期趋势、傅里叶季节项和人口偏移的负二项式模型来分析 死亡率 数据。敏感性分析检查了不同的时间分层和建模方法。
elements_zh.main_results: 大流行前,甲型流感占 死亡率 的 1.8%(95% CI 1.4-2.3%),而乙型流感没有显示出可检测到的影响。在整个大流行期间,SARS-CoV-2 占死亡人数的 6.1%(95% CI 4.2-8.0%),比大流行前的甲型流感负担高出约 4 倍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,尽管有对策,但 SARS-CoV-2 与 死亡率 人群负担显着高于 季节性流感 A 相关。

elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究对甲型流感和 RSV 的估计对季节性调整很敏感,表明基于模型选择的结果存在潜在的变异性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道病毒是 死亡率 群体的主要贡献者,但死因编码低估了其影响。将病毒循环与 死亡率 波动联系起来的生态回归模型可以解决这一限制。目的 估计加拿大安大略省(1993-2025 年)与甲型和乙型流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 死亡率 的人群归因分数 (PAF),并描述大流行过渡期间病毒归因 死亡率 的时间变化。方法 我们利用实验室 监测 指标分析了甲型、乙型、RSV 和 SARS-CoV-2 流感的每月全因 死亡率 数据。具有长期趋势、傅里叶季节性项和人口偏移的负二项式模型适合大流行前(1993年1月至2020年2月)和大流行合并时期(2020年3月至2025年2月)。PAF 源自将病毒系数设置为零的反事实预测。敏感性分析检查了大流行期间的时间分层(国际关注的突发公共卫生事件 [PHEIC] 期间:2020 年 3 月至 2023 年 4 月;PHEIC 后:2023 年 5 月至 2025 年 2 月),排除了大流行早期(2020 年 3 月至 6 月),以及没有傅里叶季节调整的模型。Wald 测试比较了不同规格的系数。结果 大流行前,甲型流感占 死亡率 的 1.8%(95% CI 1.4–2.3%);乙型流感没有显示出可检测到的影响。RSV 在经季节性调整的模型中表现出负相关,但在未经季节调整的情况下呈正相关(PAF 1.9%,95% CI 1.3–2.4%)。在整个大流行期间(2020年3月至2025年2月;n=60个月),在基线死亡率升高(IRR 1.050,P=0.027)的情况下,SARS-CoV-2占死亡人数的6.1%(95% CI 4.2-8.0%),大约是大流行前甲型流感负担的4倍,尽管疫苗接种和抗病毒药物 可用性。模型估计的 SARS-CoV-2 死亡人数与同期安大略省公共卫生部门报告的 COVID-19 死亡人数非常吻合。时间分层发现,PHEIC 后时期 SARS-CoV-2 归因的 死亡率 显着增加(PAF 9.8%,95% CI 1.1-17.7%;p=0.027),而 PHEIC 后甲型和 B 型流感归因分数与大流行前的基线没有显着差异。排除 2020 年 3 月至 6 月,保守的 SARS-CoV-2 PAF 为 5.7%(95% CI 3.3-8.1%),证实了初步估计的稳健性。荟萃分析显示,不同建模方法中甲型流感 (I2=92.8%) 和 RSV (I2=89.1%) 存在显着异质性,但 SARS-CoV-2 异质性极小 (I2=5.5%)。结论 尽管有可用的对策,但 SARS-CoV-2 与 死亡率 人群负担比 季节性流感 A 高 3-4 倍相关。PHEIC 后的数据表明,呼吸道病毒 死亡率(包括流感病毒)的负担尚未恢复到大流行前的水平,这凸显了呼吸道病毒预防策略的持续重要性。甲型流感和 RSV 的估计对季节性调整敏感,突出了在量化病毒归因 死亡率 时建模选择的重要性。

title: Dairy cattle movement networks govern the spread and persistence of H5N1 B3.13 in the United States
abstract: Avian influenza virus H5N1 is predominantly found in wild and domestic birds. H5N1 genotype B3.13 was first detected in United States dairy cattle in March 2024 and spread through much of the country during 2024 and 2025, resulting in the largest known H5N1 outbreak in domestic mammals. By analysing viral genomic data jointly with historical cattle movement patterns, we find that live cattle movement is the predominant contributor to H5N1 spatial spread, rather than wild or domestic birds. Using phylogeographic methods we estimate that >40% of interstate viral transmissions occurred before B3.13's first detection and >70% occurred before interstate dairy cattle movement restrictions were implemented in April 2024. After this implementation, interstate transmission slowed but within-state spread persisted, driven by local cattle network density and movement volume. Our epidemic simulations demonstrate that the connectivity of counties within and around the Texas Panhandle - where the earliest cases were documented - predisposed the region to become an outbreak epicentre. Counterfactual simulations indicate that interstate restrictions needed to have begun 2-3 months earlier in order to limit the epizootic substantively, given the extent of cryptic spread before detection. Network-informed interventions outperformed geographically-defined containment, but response speed (rather than intervention strength) was the limiting factor in our epidemic models, underscoring the need for surveillance systems capable of detecting pathogen emergence before widespread dissemination.

title: Air sampling for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural Zambia: a prospective comparison with human surveillance
abstract: Respiratory infections are the leading cause of acute disease incidence globally and disproportionately burden low- and middle-income countries where surveillance capacity is limited. While facility-based surveillance remains the standard for respiratory pathogen monitoring in human populations, environmental air sampling offers potential advantages as a non-invasive supplementary method. We conducted a prospective environmental air sampling study nested within ongoing respiratory disease surveillance at Macha Hospital in Southern Province, Zambia, from July 2025 to June 2026. Air samplers were deployed continuously in the outpatient department and three inpatient wards, with filters collected and tested three times weekly. Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen's Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.5; Spearman's rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.2; Spearman's rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

title_zh: 赞比亚农村地区设施呼吸道病原体 监测 的空气采样:与人类 监测 的前瞻性比较
source_body_en: Respiratory infections are the leading cause of acute disease incidence globally and disproportionately burden low- and middle-income countries where surveillance capacity is limited. While facility-based surveillance remains the standard for respiratory pathogen monitoring in human populations, environmental air sampling offers potential advantages as a non-invasive supplementary method. We conducted a prospective environmental air sampling study nested within ongoing respiratory disease surveillance at Macha Hospital in Southern Province, Zambia, from July 2025 to June 2026. Air samplers were deployed continuously in the outpatient department and three inpatient wards, with filters collected and tested three times weekly. Surveillance in the patient population was conducted year-round with nasopharyngeal samples collected from patients with influenza-like illness. All samples were tested for influenza A/B virus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 using the Cepheid GeneXpert platform. We analyzed concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples using percent agreement, Cohen's Kappa, Spearman correlations, and logistic regression with generalized estimating equations. Over 12 months, 596 air samples and 701 human samples were analyzed. Influenza A virus was the most common pathogen, detected in 38 air samples and 87 nasopharyngeal samples, with most cases detected from July to September 2025. For Influenza A, there was strong same-week concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (80.4% overall agreement; 44.4% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.5; Spearman's rho = 0.57). SARS-CoV-2 was also common, detected in 18 air samples and 16 nasopharyngeal samples, with cases detected sporadically throughout the year. For SARS-CoV-2, there was limited concordance between air and nasopharyngeal samples (68.6% agreement; 23.8% positive agreement; Cohen's Kappa = 0.2; Spearman's rho = 0.2). Influenza B virus (1 air and 13 nasopharyngeal samples positive) and RSV (0 air and 4 nasopharyngeal samples positive) circulated sporadically, and unsurprisingly, gave limited concordance between samples. Cycle threshold values for influenza A virus (median for target 1: 36.7 vs. 25.1; p<0.001; median for target 2: 39.5 vs. 28.6; p<0.001) and SARS-CoV-2 (median: 41.3 vs. 27.5; p<0.001) were significantly higher for positive air samples than for nasopharyngeal samples. Implementation challenges were documented, including intermittent power outages and compromised electrical outlets causing sampler shutdowns, as well as study awareness issues that required sensitization activities for both facility staff and patients. Air sampling was feasible and demonstrated promise as a supplementary method for facility-based respiratory pathogen surveillance in rural resource-limited settings. These findings support integrating environmental air sampling alongside surveillance in patient populations as part of a multimodal approach to respiratory pathogen monitoring.

title: The relationship between the oral health status and COVID-19 and Influenza infections
abstract: Abstract A relationship has been reported between oral hygiene and influenza infection. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and influenza are major respiratory virus infections. The oral cavity may act as both an entry site and reservoir for these viruses. The present study examined the role of oral health in SARS-CoV-2 infection through epidemiology and histopathology. A prospective observational study was also conducted to investigate whether good oral hygiene habits contribute to the prevention of respiratory viral infections. In the epidemiological study using data from health/dental check-ups and the Japanese National Health Insurance database, a multivariate analysis identified poor oral hygiene as an independent risk factor for the onset of COVID-19. A histopathological analysis revealed that the expression of the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor and furin in the gingival epithelium was higher with than without inflammation. The prospective observational study comparing two groups with different oral hygiene habits suggested that good oral hygiene practices with interdental brushes and mouthwash prevented the onset of COVID-19 and influenza. Collectively, these results indicate that poor oral hygiene contributes to the onset of COVID-19 infection by increasing ACE2 and furin expression. Furthermore, improvements in oral hygiene may prevent the onset of COVID-19 and influenza.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了保持口腔卫生作为预防呼吸道病毒感染(包括流感)的潜在预防措施的重要性。
